judged_text: Per-destination targeting is implemented only in GoogleCalendarService; BaseCalendarService (Apple/CalDav and its subclasses), Lark and Office365 still resolve the target from destinationCalendar[0] and ignore the per-destination credentialId/externalId that the new createAllCalendarEvents loop passes. For collective multi-host bookings on non-Google providers, iterations beyond the first host request destination[0]'s calendar with a different host's credentials — CalDav's filter matches none of its calendars (silent no-op) and Lark/O365 get an API error that CalendarManager swallows — so the other hosts' calendar events are silently never created.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `destinationCalendar` to an array and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now loops over each destination calendar, calling `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` (packages/core/EventManager.ts). However, only GoogleCalendarService actually targets the right destination per credential by selecting `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)` (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts). Other providers (BaseCalendarService/CalDav, Lark, Office365) still derive the target calendar from the first element (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`) and ignore which destination is currently being processed, so iterations for additional hosts will still attempt to create/update/delete against destinationCalendar[0]'s externalId with a different host's credential (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts, packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts). This makes multi-destination (e.g., COLLECTIVE) event creation incorrect for non-Google providers, consistent with the finding’s described outcome.
